code.text: Early 2-hour 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (gestational diabetes screening, overweight + chronic hypertension)

resource.patientInstruction: Please complete the early glucose (sugar) tolerance blood test to check for gestational diabetes.

code.text: Home blood pressure monitoring program (measure and log BP)

resource.patientInstruction: Check your blood pressure at home at least twice a week (more if advised) and record the readings to review with your care team.

code.text: Referral for behavioral health / mental health and psychosocial support assessment (history of chronic stress)

resource.patientInstruction: Please attend a behavioral health visit to review stress, mood, coping, and support during pregnancy.

code.text: Referral to Maternal-Fetal Medicine (high-risk obstetrics) for chronic hypertension in pregnancy

resource.patientInstruction: Please schedule and attend a visit with the high-risk pregnancy (Maternal-Fetal Medicine) specialist.

code.text: Preeclampsia surveillance laboratory panel (CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel/LFTs, serum creatinine, uric acid, urine protein:creatinine ratio)

resource.patientInstruction: Please complete periodic blood and urine tests so we can watch for early signs of preeclampsia.

code.text: Referral to dietitian for nutrition counseling and healthy gestational weight gain (BMI 29.6)

resource.patientInstruction: Please attend a nutrition visit to plan healthy eating and appropriate weight gain in pregnancy.

resource.description: Attend nutrition counseling and follow the gestational weight-gain plan.
Attend the behavioral health / mental health and support assessment.
Complete the early oral glucose tolerance test (gestational diabetes screening).
Take low-dose aspirin (81 mg) by mouth every evening until advised to stop.
Schedule and attend the Maternal-Fetal Medicine (high-risk pregnancy) consultation.
Measure blood pressure at home at least twice weekly and log the readings for your care team.

Learn the warning signs of preeclampsia (severe/persistent headache, vision changes, upper-right belly pain, sudden swelling of face/hands, shortness of breath) and seek urgent care immediately if they occur.
